punchline: According to Taleb, your bones actually need stress to stay strong; take the load away and they weaken.
thirty_sec: When you lift something heavy, you do small damage to the muscle. Your body answers by overcompensating and rebuilding it stronger. Nassim Taleb calls this hormesis, and he says it only works with the right dose: short bursts of stress, then rest. Constant pressure harms instead. His bigger point is that protecting something from every stress can leave it weaker, not safer.
question: What's something in your life that got stronger because it was pushed rather than protected?
key_contrast: Surviving stress versus growing from it
